claim: Wolfram MathWorld's Egyptian Fraction article confirms Guy's Unsolved Problems in Number Theory (2nd ed., 1994) Section D11 'Egyptian Fractions' occupies pp. 158-166 and is the standard reference point for the Erdos-Straus and Sierpinski unit-fraction conjectures.
stance_target: bibliographic provenance of Guy's UPINT section on Egyptian fractions
quoted_support: Guy, R. K. "Egyptian Fractions." §D11 in Unsolved Problems in Number Theory, 2nd ed. New York: Springer-Verlag, pp. 158-166, 1994.

claim: Paul Erdos proved in 1932 that the sum of reciprocals of any number of equally-spaced integers is never itself a reciprocal, a rigidity result about single sums, not about pairs of triples matched on two symmetric functions.
stance_target: prior art for Section 5's two-triple equal-sum-and-equal-reciprocal-sum problem
quoted_support: In 1932, Erdős proved that the sum of the reciprocals of any number of equally spaced integers is never a reciprocal.

claim: The Erdos-Straus conjecture (4/n=1/a+1/b+1/c always solvable) and Sierpinski's analogous 5/n conjecture are the article's two named open unit-fraction-equation conjectures; neither imposes any equal-integer-sum condition across two distinct triples.
stance_target: existence of a named prior conjecture matching Section 5's exact two-symmetric-function pairing condition
quoted_support: Paul Erdős and E. G. Straus have conjectured that the Diophantine equation ... always can be solved, an assertion sometimes known as the Erdős-Straus conjecture, and Sierpiński (1956) conjectured that ... can be solved (Guy 1994).
